sections.h2: Recording a deed in Armstrong County
sections.html:
The Register and Recorder handles deeds, from Suite 102 of the courthouse at 500 E. Market Street, Kittanning. One office holds three jobs: Recorder of Deeds, Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans’ Court. The main number is (724) 548-3280.

Transactions are taken from 8:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m., while records research runs until 4:15 p.m. Payment is by cash or check only. Cards of any kind are refused.

On the recorder’s side, the office keeps real estate records safe and files land documents, veterans’ discharges, notary bonds and commissions, and powers of attorney that deal with real estate.

A deed can be recorded electronically or on paper. Four e-recording vendors are listed: Simplifile, CSC Recording, ePN and Indecomm. A title company already using one of them can send a deed without a courier.

Staff check each document against a fixed list before accepting it.

  • The document date has to fall on or before the acknowledgment date.
  • Deeds and mortgages need a legal description that names the municipality, county and state.
  • A tax map number is required. It is not the same as a parcel number, and the Mapping Department, at (724) 548-3234, can supply it.
  • The acknowledgment needs the notary’s signature, a readable stamp and the expiration date.
  • A Certificate of Residence must be completed and signed.
  • Documents with shaded areas are not recorded.

Fees are not refunded, so the amount has to be right the first time. When several documents belong to one transaction, each page must show the intended recording order, and any re-recording expense caused by wrong order falls on whoever submitted them.

The tax is 1% for the state and another 1% for the local governments and school district. Each is paid on a separate check, with a third check for the filing fee. All three are written to the Recorder of Deeds.

A Statement of Value, filed in duplicate, is needed in three situations: the full price is missing from the deed, the deed is a gift or has no consideration, or an exemption is claimed. It is also needed for rights of way and easements. A transfer that is wholly exempt on family grounds does not require one, provided the relationship is written on the deed. The office forwards one copy to the Department of Revenue.

A deed that names a price of $1.00 triggers the form, because the real value is not shown. When land spans more than one municipality, the deed must state each one’s percentage so the local tax divides correctly.

The state can revisit a sale later. If an investigator decides the property was worth more than stated, or that an exemption was invalid, the Department of Revenue sends a determination directly to the parties, collects the extra tax and interest itself, and issues a receipt for the recorder to file.

The recorder’s fee schedule is posted as a PDF on the county’s Register and Recorder page. Ask the office for the current sheet before closing.

The Common Level Ratio changes each July 1, so ask the office which factor applies to the date on your deed.

Record searches are by first and last name or by book and page. The office cannot search by tax map number or street address, and its staff do not give legal advice. If you need a title history, hire a title company or an attorney.

The recorder runs a free Record Alert System through Landex, the recording vendor. Anyone who signs up gets an email whenever a document is recorded under their name, and businesses can sign up as well.

The same Landex site holds the county’s records for people who search often. A paid remote subscription suits frequent users and a pay-per-document web store suits occasional ones. Landex sets those charges, not the county. Owners who inherit or sell land here can use the alert to catch an unexpected deed or mortgage.

Kittanning is the county seat, and the Allegheny River runs through the county. Population is 63,698 as of July 2025, with 32,314 housing units. About 78.8% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $157,300. Median household income is $65,008. With so many owner-occupied houses, most buyers choose among existing homes.

sections.h2: Documents to bring on closing day
sections.html: Before anyone drives to Kittanning, make sure the packet has a notarized deed with a legal description, the tax map number, a signed Certificate of Residence, and three checks: state tax, local tax and filing fee. Add a Statement of Value in duplicate if the deed has no price, is a gift, or claims an exemption. Cash is accepted, but checks are easier to trace if a question comes up later.

sections.h2: What a cash sale does not change
sections.html: Selling for cash does not skip the recorder. The deed is still checked, taxed and filed here. What a cash deal removes is the buyer’s loan approval, which is often the slowest piece of a closing. If a mortgage is being paid off from your proceeds, ask the title company to confirm that the release is recorded afterward.

faqs.q: Where is the Armstrong County Recorder of Deeds office?
faqs.a: It is inside the Register and Recorder’s office, Suite 102 of the Armstrong County Courthouse at 500 E. Market Street, Kittanning, PA 16201. The telephone is (724) 548-3280.

faqs.q: Can I pay with a credit card at the Armstrong County recorder?
faqs.a: No. The office accepts cash or check only. Plan checks ahead for the state tax, the local tax and the filing fee.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available for Armstrong County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, CSC Recording, ePN and Indecomm are the listed vendors, so title companies using any of them can submit a deed electronically.

faqs.q: What is a tax map number and why does a deed need one?
faqs.a: It identifies the property in the county’s mapping system and has to appear on deeds and mortgages. It is not the parcel number. The Mapping Department at (724) 548-3234 can provide it.

faqs.q: Do I need a Statement of Value to record a deed?
faqs.a: You need one if the deed omits the full price, is a gift, or claims an exemption, and it must be filed in duplicate. A transfer wholly exempt because of family ties does not need one when the relationship appears on the deed.
